inputs.notes: Cash & Investments $1,566M and Total Debt $988.6M as of Q2 FY2026 (Dec 31, 2025). Net Debt is negative (net cash position of $577.4M). Last FCF is FY2025 full-year free cash flow.

historical_growth.eps_note: GAAP EPS negative throughout due to heavy SBC ($26-27% of revenue). Cannot compute meaningful CAGR. EPS improved from -$2.05 (FY2022) to -$0.98 (FY2025) in magnitude but remains negative. FCF used as primary profitability metric.
historical_growth.equity_note: Equity 3Y CAGR is unusually high (60%) due to large GAAP losses in FY2022 depressing the starting base. Equity 5Y CAGR of 18.5% is more representative but still distorted by SBC-driven net losses. Not used as primary rate per company instructions.
historical_growth.growth_rate_rationale: Per company-specific instructions, FCF CAGR is the primary metric for TEAM (not equity CAGR), as GAAP net losses from SBC make equity growth unreliable. The FCF 3-year CAGR of 23.6% aligns closely with revenue growth (23.0% 3Y CAGR) and management guidance of 20%+ through FY2027. Selected as the representative growth rate, with scenarios modeled above and below this.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3Y CAGR (60.2%) diverges significantly from Revenue 3Y CAGR (23.0%) — gap of 37.2pp. This is due to the artificially depressed FY2022 equity base ($327M) from GAAP net losses. Equity CAGR is not used for DCF; FCF CAGR is the selected primary metric. No divergence concern between FCF and Revenue CAGRs (0.6pp gap).

base.description: ~20% FCF growth in Year 1 decelerating to 12% by Year 5, reflecting management's 20%+ revenue guidance through FY2027 with gradual normalization. FCF grows slightly faster than revenue to capture margin expansion from 27% to ~30%. WACC 10% appropriate for high-growth tech with strong FCF but SBC dilution risk.

bull.description: Cloud migration accelerates, AI monetization via Rovo drives incremental revenue, enterprise sales motion matures. RPO growth of 44% YoY signals multi-year commitment. FCF growth 27% Y1 declining to 16% Y5. Lower WACC reflects reduced risk as cloud mix exceeds 80%. Aligns with bull case: Teamwork Graph moat, AI reinforcing competitive position, $67B TAM underpenetration.

bear.description: Data Center revenue cliff in FY27 creates near-term headwind, Microsoft bundling pressure intensifies, enterprise GTM transition stumbles amid leadership turnover. FCF growth moderates to 13% Y1 declining to 4% Y5. Higher WACC reflects elevated execution risk. FCF margin remains flat at 25% as AI infrastructure costs and enterprise sales ramp pressure opex. Aligns with bear case: DC revenue cliff, GTM transition risk, Microsoft competitive threat.

sensitivity.note: Matrix uses base case FCF growth rates [20%, 18%, 16%, 14%, 12%] applied from FY2025 FCF of $1,415.5M. Net cash of $577.4M added to equity value. All values in USD per share.

key_investment_considerations.primary_value_driver: Cloud migration and expanding FCF margins. TEAM generated $1.4B FCF on $5.2B revenue (27% margin) in FY2025. The 2029 Data Center EOL deadline creates a multi-year structural tailwind for cloud growth.
key_investment_considerations.key_risk: Data Center revenue cliff in FY27 when EOL recognition pull-forward unwinds. Simultaneously managing PLG-to-enterprise GTM transition with leadership turnover (President, CFO both departing).
key_investment_considerations.current_price_assessment: At $68.81, TEAM trades at ~50% of base case IV ($137.60) and is below the base case entry price for a 15% CAGR ($82.32). Even in the bear case, IV of $76.02 is above the current price with 10.5% upside, suggesting the stock is pricing in worse-than-bear-case outcomes. The probability-weighted IV of $142.09 implies 106% upside.
key_investment_considerations.moat_assessment: Strong switching costs via Jira/Confluence workflow embedding, proprietary Teamwork Graph (100B+ objects) as AI data moat, Marketplace ecosystem network effects. These factors support above-average terminal growth rate assumptions.
key_investment_considerations.wacc_rationale: 10% base WACC reflects: risk-free rate ~4.3%, equity risk premium ~5%, beta ~1.1 for high-growth enterprise SaaS. Lower WACC (9%) in bull case as cloud mix and enterprise commitments (RPO +44% YoY) reduce business risk. Higher WACC (12%) in bear case for execution risk during GTM transition.
